meta.title: Platform · {brand}
meta.description: Hardware-agnostic ingest, versioned and comparable preprocessing pipelines, provenance for every run, and a governed model registry. Built and tested internally; not deployed yet.

hero.heading: Reproducible, comparable pipelines, from electrode to model.
hero.lede: Every run is pinned to a pipeline version and records every parameter, version and input hash. Compare pipelines side by side instead of trusting one cleaning default.

sections.heading: Preprocessing choices change results.
body: There is no single correct way to clean a neural recording. The published evidence says the choice of pipeline moves the answer, so the pipeline has to be recorded, versioned and comparable.

evidence.text: In a 2025 study, every artifact-correction step reduced decoding performance, while higher high-pass cutoffs increased it.
A 2025 comparison of 43 preprocessing pipelines found no single best pipeline.
A systematic review of 129 EEG-BCI publications found code or pipeline availability in 20.9% of them.

sections.heading: Hardware-agnostic ingest.
body: Connectors for EEG, ECoG and microelectrode recordings in open formats. Recordings are stored on standard time-series infrastructure; we compete on provenance, not on storage.

items.heading: Open formats
items.body: EDF/BDF, BrainVision, XDF and BIDS import, with typed errors for corrupt files. NWB import is written but not yet tested.

items.heading: Streaming
items.body: Lab Streaming Layer (LSL) input for real-time sessions, tested on a single host.

items.heading: Existing tools
items.body: Integrations with MNE-Python, BrainFlow and the BIDS and NWB tooling your lab already uses.

sections.heading: Versioned pipelines with full provenance.
body: Versioned preprocessing pipelines with full provenance. Run one, or run a grid of them and see how your results move.

items.heading: Pinned versions
items.body: A run names an exact pipeline version, so it can be repeated later.

items.heading: Provenance graph
items.body: Inputs, parameters, versions and outputs are linked, from raw recording to trained model.

items.heading: Pipeline grids
items.body: Run a grid of pipelines on one dataset and see how decoding metrics shift across them.

sections.heading: A governed model registry.
body: Governed model registry, built and tested internally but not deployed: versioned models with provenance, documented intended use and use restrictions. Benchmarks will be published with methods.
Models whose outputs drive a clinical or assistive device are likely to be regulated as device software in the customer's product. The registry is built to document that boundary, not to blur it.

items.heading: Intended use and restrictions
items.body: Each model records what it is for and where it must not be deployed.

items.heading: Component disclosure
items.body: Model components listed for customers' software documentation.

evidence.text: Our planning assumption, not legal advice: outputs that drive a clinical or assistive BCI are likely device software in the customer's product, which then carries the regulatory submission.
